newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes easier in two-way Hong Kong trade.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes easier in two-way Hong Kong trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed easier on Monday from New York's Friday close in two-way trade as late selling offset early physical demand, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$343.20/70 an ounce against New York's US$343.80/344.30 close on Friday and Saturday's local close of US$344.20/70.

"Early physical demand boosted gold to a day's high of US$344.00/50 but selling interest in the afternoon session depressed gold to a day's low of US$343.00/50," said a dealer at a local securities house.
"We will just keep watching the U.S. dollar moves," another dealer said. "I think gold will hold at around US$343 to $345 in the short term."
Local gold ended HK$9 lower at HK$3,175 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its Saturday fix at -4.00.
